phenomenon: Completed daily observed Binance forced-liquidation stress identifies an already known deleveraging episode. Subsequent 4h price acceptance or reclaim may distinguish continuation from reversal after conservative publication lag.
economic_behavioral_mechanism: Margin-constrained participants close urgently. Some effects may persist after a stress day has completed and its daily aggregate is available. Subsequent confirmed structure can distinguish persistent repricing from temporary dislocation. Daily aggregation does not recover intraday cascade timing; the surviving delayed edge, if any, must be tested.

participants.forced_actor: Leveraged holders subject to margin calls or involuntary liquidation
participants.edge_provider: Price-insensitive forced closers and liquidity takers requiring immediate execution
participants.edge_consumer: Patient, risk-constrained entrant waiting for post-event structure

persistence: Forced execution and temporarily constrained market-maker inventories can outlast instantaneous arbitrage; whether enough delay remains after hourly confirmation is the main empirical question.
crowding_decay: Faster absorption, improved arbitrage or crowded reclaim/pullback entries can consume the effect before confirmation and make net expectancy nonpositive.
direction: Conditional long and short: continuation follows the extreme move after acceptance; reversal opposes it after reclaim; ambiguous structure means no trade.
expression: Binance USDT linear perpetuals on BTC, ETH, SOL and AAVE only; isolated margin; three risk-budgeted entries in later lifecycle stage.

holding_horizon.clock: From first fill; never reset by additions; stops may close immediately

expected_signal_frequency.unit: independent market episodes per month across all four assets
expected_signal_frequency.basis: Inherited ex ante prediction; daily detection plus publication lag may make it fail. No observed candidate frequency or return used to set it.

payoff.qualitative_shape: Reversal returns capped by recovery target; continuation potentially right-skewed, with trailing giveback; gaps can lose more than 1R. R is initial tranche risk for core and frozen total position risk for staged comparisons; both also report dollars.

expected_to_work: Liquidation pressure with subsequent stable absorption
Persistent directional order flow distinguishable by post-shock acceptance
expected_to_fail: Repeated alternating breakouts in illiquid chop
Confirmation delay consumes the entire dislocation
Missing or changing forced-order feed coverage

failure_invalidation_mechanism: After costs and episode dependence, acceptance/reclaim routing fails to improve over fixed-direction controls or fails across chronological blocks; alternatively required forced-flow evidence cannot be sourced with adequate availability and outage provenance.

availability.rule: Completed Binance 4h and 1h bars only; next 1m open strictly after decision; raw bytes and revision receipts required.
Base-quantity OI timestamp strictly before decision; lag by at least one 5m interval; maximum staleness 10m. Archive publication is not historical availability proof.

Coinalyze Binance-specific daily USD long/short totals: bucket [t,t+24h); modeled availability t+48h. This is a disclosed development assumption, not verified historical publication. Never use intraday or incomplete-day aggregate.
Actual settlement times and rates, including zero rates; cost or receipt on live quantity at settlement, not a fixed 8h schedule.
Historical mark path, maintenance brackets, quantity filters and effective fees; isolated collateral replay on every fill/settlement. Retrospective assumptions disclosed separately.
Later-stage daily equity proxy only. Last independently timestamped available close, conservatively one additional US session lag; archive without availability provenance stays development-only.
Global account and top-trader position ratios kept separate; same 5m lag and 10m staleness rule as OI. Descriptive only in v001.

falsifier.test: Score-free one-entry model using fixed structural routing, evaluated against always-continue and always-reverse controls on the same eligible confirmed decisions. No macro or staging in the core test. Separate forced-flow contribution diagnostic compares with predeclared price-plus-OI-only event selection; it never becomes a replacement liquidation strategy without a new version.
falsifier.null: Routing has no positive incremental net expectancy over the better unconditional direction control after shared event/time-block correction.
falsifier.inconclusive_rule: Insufficient episodes or unavailable physical/PIT data yields INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE/BLOCKED, never proof the mechanism is false.
